answers.source: Curio's one-view rule in its own words, utk_curio/frontend/urban-workflows/src/contracts/autkGrammar.json oneView, pinned by utk_curio/backend/tests/test_agents/test_document_validation.py::TestOneViewPerNode; the stations' ada values and their node as docs/examples/dataflows/chicago-loop-layers.json node d517325b-266b-575d-ab48-2685bb889536's content maps them (its CTA station layer, getFnv ada) and node 5abae988-9ecb-5f71-85cc-958df3999990's content returns them
answers.reply:
I left this map's document as it is. An Autark node draws one view: one map or one plot. Put each in its own Autark node, and link them with interaction edges.

So the bar chart goes in an Autark node of its own: add an Autark node, connect the CTA 'L' stations node to it, and give it a document with one plot, "mark": "bar" over the stations' ada values (accessible, not accessible or unknown). Then link the two views with an interaction edge, so picking stations in one highlights them in the other.
